page.layout: One printed page. Running text in a single column, with marginal notes in the right margin. Running head at top, page number at top right, catchword at bottom right, gathering signature at bottom left.

main_text.l: unquam suspicabitur. Quid ergo est? Ni-
mirum Tertullianus, quæ nondum suo
tempore extabant, quę non nisi diu post e-
jus fata natæ sunt Constitutiones, eas
quantumvis acer ac diligens vel perspi-
cere, vel è futuri temporis tenebris eruere
non potuit. Nihil mirum est, quod
quæ non erant, minimè animadverterit. Cæ-
terum nodum hunc, nisi eas nondum tunc
fuisse concesseris, nunquam expedies. Huc
quoque pertinet, quod cum alibi {a}mulieres
à conferendo baptismo longissime idem
submoveat; Διαλαγεῶν [?] disertissimam in
eam rem sententiam nullus in eo loco me-
moravit.
Quid quod non in his modo, sed & in
aliis quoque causis eadem semper cernitur
Tertulliani stultitia, idemque stupor? præsens,
paratumque Bovianorum Apostolo-
rum præsidium ubique constantissime ta-
fti-dientis? Nam & alibi {c}dum adversus Ca-
tholicos stata Montani jejunia, serasque &
ad vesperam dilatas escas, denique & Xero-
phagias magno molimine defendit, nul-
lum de Bovii Apostolis, qui Montani in
hac causa pene toti sunt, verbum fecit; de
tam multis eorum pro Montano sententiis
nullam attulit. Extat ejus adversus Psychi-
cos (quo nomine Catholicos invidiose ap-
pellat) de jejuniis liber, in quo id inprimis
probare

marginalia.note: c l. de jejun. adv. Psych.

page.notes: Marginal notes a, b and c are printed in small italic type beside the text. The Greek word in line 6 of the first paragraph is uncertain. Its letters were read as Διαλαγεῶν and may be Διαλογεῶν. The reference marks a and c are shown in braces at the points where they stand in the text. The catchword and signature are at the foot.
